example.title: Decision Framework
example.code:
✅ Data Analytics is for you if:
  • You love asking "why is this number moving?"
  • You enjoy Excel, dashboards, and clean tables
  • You're comfortable with SQL (or want to be)
  • You want $70k–$180k+ without a CS degree
  • You like translating data into business stories

❌ Consider other roles if:
  • You want to build software systems → Data Engineer
  • You want to ship ML models → Data Scientist
  • You want to design experiments → Product Analyst / DS

📊 Your first test: complete Phase 1 (Excel + 1 dashboard).
   If it feels fun, you're on the right track.

example.title: Top 5 Products by Revenue + MoM Growth
example.code:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    product,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
    SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct/100.0)) AS revenue
  FROM retail_orders
  WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY product, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)
)
SELECT
  product,
  month,
  revenue,
  LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY product ORDER BY month) AS prev_rev,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY product ORDER BY month))
         / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY product ORDER BY month), 0),
  1) AS mom_growth_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month DESC, revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- | product               | month       | revenue | prev_rev | mom % |
-- |-----------------------|-------------|---------|----------|-------|
-- | Wireless Headphones X3| 2026-01-01  |  84,210 |  61,400  | +37.1 |
-- | Smart Watch S2        | 2026-01-01  |  52,980 |  49,100  |  +7.9 |
-- | Bluetooth Speaker     | 2026-01-01  |  41,330 |  44,800  |  -7.7 |

example.title: Pandas — Same Top-Products Question
example.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("retail_orders.csv", parse_dates=["order_date"])
df["revenue"] = df["quantity"] * df["unit_price"] * (1 - df["discount_pct"]/100)

monthly = (
    df[df.order_date >= "2025-10-01"]
      .assign(month=lambda d: d.order_date.dt.to_period("M"))
      .groupby(["product", "month"], as_index=False)["revenue"].sum()
      .sort_values(["product", "month"])
)

monthly["mom_growth_pct"] = (
    monthly.groupby("product")["revenue"]
           .pct_change()
           .mul(100).round(1)
)

top = (monthly[monthly.month == monthly.month.max()]
         .nlargest(5, "revenue"))
print(top)

#                   product     month   revenue  mom_growth_pct
# 0  Wireless Headphones X3  2026-01   84210.0           37.1
# 1          Smart Watch S2  2026-01   52980.0            7.9
# 2       Bluetooth Speaker  2026-01   41330.0           -7.7

lesson.overview: Bad models are why dashboards are slow and wrong. A clean star schema (1 fact table, many dimension tables) makes Power BI and Tableau both 10× faster and 10× easier to extend.
Power BI is the #1 BI tool in Europe and most enterprises. Master Power Query (clean data), the data model (star schema), DAX (measures), and visuals.

example.title: DAX — Sales KPIs for the Dashboard
example.code:
Total Revenue =
SUMX( fact_orders, fact_orders[quantity]
      * fact_orders[unit_price]
      * ( 1 - fact_orders[discount_pct] / 100 ) )

Revenue LY =
CALCULATE( [Total Revenue],
           SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR( dim_date[date] ) )

YoY % =
DIVIDE( [Total Revenue] - [Revenue LY], [Revenue LY] )

YTD Revenue =
TOTALYTD( [Total Revenue], dim_date[date] )

Avg Order Value =
DIVIDE( [Total Revenue], DISTINCTCOUNT( fact_orders[order_id] ) )

Top Region =
CALCULATE( SELECTEDVALUE( dim_store[region] ),
           TOPN( 1, VALUES( dim_store[region] ), [Total Revenue] ) )

/* ─ Dashboard wires these into:
     • KPI cards: Revenue, YoY %, AOV, Top Region
     • Line chart: Revenue vs LY by month
     • Matrix: Region × Category with conditional formatting
     • Slicers: Channel, Date range, Store */

phases.description: A dashboard nobody reads is worthless. Learn enough stats to not mislead the business, and enough design to make execs act. This is what unlocks senior pay.

lesson.overview: You don't need to be a statistician — but you must know mean vs median vs mode, distributions, confidence intervals, and A/B test reading. Otherwise you'll mislead the business.

example.title: AOV — Don't report just the mean
example.code:
Region: UK&I — 1,842 orders in Jan 2026

  Mean Order Value :  £124.30
  Median Order Value: £ 68.50   ← typical customer
  P90 Order Value   : £312.00
  Max Order Value   : £4,980.00 (1 big B2B order)

⚠️  Reporting only the mean hides that the typical
    customer spends £68. The mean is dragged up by
    a few huge orders.

✅  Always report median + P90 for skewed metrics
    (revenue, latency, session length, etc.)

lesson.overview: A dashboard nobody reads is worthless. Learn what to put above the fold, how to use color with meaning, and how to write a 1-sentence insight under every chart.
checklist: Always add a 1-line insight + date stamp
